subject: Capacity commit buffer & approval for AtlasHealth deal
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara@atlashealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Reid <thomas.reid@atlashealth.ai>, procurement@atlashealth.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing protection question

Marissa —

Thanks again for the detailed proposal and the committed capacity numbers. Before we lock term and SKU mix, procurement has one outstanding concern: given recent GPU price swings, can Redwood offer a mechanism to limit AtlasHealth's downside if spot/market prices rise sharply during the 24-month commit?

Concretely, procurement asked whether there is an optional "cost buffer" (credit or conditional discount) that triggers if our effective unit cost exceeds a defined threshold tied to a published GPU index. They're not asking for full pass-through, but something to keep our unit economics predictable during model rollouts.

We're hoping to avoid adding complex contingent adjustments into the SOW, but procurement needs something in writing or a clear playbook for executive review. Attaching our procurement questionnaire for reference.

Can you outline a couple of clean options (no more than 2) we could include in the deal? If so, Thomas and I can present to the CFO next week.

Best,
Sara

Attachment: AtlasHealth_Procurement_Qs.pdf (survey, 4 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing protection question

Ben/Karthik — forwarding AtlasHealth's procurement note. They want a lightweight protection against GPU market shocks. They asked for up to two clean options we can negotiate into the SOW.

Quick context: AtlasHealth is targeting a 24-month reserved commit across our Aurora T4/T6 mix, with burst allowances. Deal size is mid-enterprise (estimated $3.2M ARR if exercised). Finance has previously pushed back on open-ended pass-throughs.

I sketched two options in the attached spreadsheet (Commit_Term_Scenarios.xlsx):
  - Option A: Fixed unit price + quarterly "safeguard credit" if a GPU index breaches a X% threshold over baseline (credit applied to next invoice, capped at Y% per quarter). Simple, predictable exposure cap.
  - Option B: Tiered price floor with a one-time true-up mechanism at 12 months if market index > threshold; customer pays reduced incremental credit vs full pass-through. Slightly more paperwork but smaller admin overhead over time.

Can you review and mark what needs legal/finance sign-off? If we can keep the maximum liability to a defined cap and state the index and calculation plainly, I think we can get this approved. Laura — can you sanity-check the numbers and call out approval path?

I want to get back to them by EOD Friday with two clean choices and recommended internal fallback.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment: Commit_Term_Scenarios.xlsx (3 scenario tabs)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing protection question

Agree with Marissa's framing. High level comments from pricing/finance:

- Option A (safeguard credit): acceptable if we cap exposure to <= 7.5% of committed spend per rolling 12-month window and tie the trigger to a published GPU spot index (we recommend "MLGPU Index" or similar).
- Option B (12-month true-up): workable only if the true-up is limited to delta above a 6% threshold and capped by a fixed dollar amount (e.g., $120k over term).

Approval path: anything that increases potential liability > $150k requires VP Finance sign-off. Anything > $350k requires CFO sign-off and legal escalation. We should model worst-case P&L impact and include it in the deal deck.

Operational note: product/ops needs to guarantee SKU substitutions and equivalent perf if underlying hardware changes. Karthik, please confirm whether Aurora T6->T8 substitutions are realistic under this deal and whether we can lock instance parity in the SOW.

I'll run the scenario sheet through finance and return with a recommended cap and trigger definition by Thursday morning.

-Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing protection question

Ben/Marissa —

Operational clarifications:

- SKU parity: we can commit to performance parity guarantees, but calls out two constraints: 1) exact GPU model may change (vendor supply), 2) quantization and compilation variance may slightly alter token throughput. We can lock to equivalent TFLOPS + memory floor rather than exact SKU to be operationally feasible.
- Burst: we'll allow a 20% burst above committed baseline for first 6 months (pilot), then review. Burst pricing should be pre-agreed in SOW to avoid surprise invoices.
- Index definition: recommend we use a 30-day rolling average of the published ML GPU Index and define baseline at contract signing. Trigger = 20% above baseline for a credit event. Calculation example included in my reply below.

I'll attach a one-pager with operational guarantees we can include as an SLO appendix. If legal wants SKU-level wording, we should push to equivalence-metric language.

-Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara@atlashealth.ai>, Thomas Reid <thomas.reid@atlashealth.ai>, procurement@atlashealth.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Dec 2028 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing protection question

Sara/Thomas —

Thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Attached are two concise, negotiable options for AtlasHealth to review. Short summary:

Option A — Safeguard Credit (recommended for simplicity):
  - Trigger: ML GPU Index 30-day avg > 20% above baseline (baseline = index at contract signature)
  - Remedy: Quarterly credit equal to 50% of the incremental unit cost above threshold, applied to next invoice
  - Cap: Credits capped at 7% of committed quarterly spend; cumulative cap of 18% of annual committed spend
  - Approval: within finance authority for up to $150k liability; anything above triggers VP Finance

Option B — 12-month True-up (recommended if Atlas prefers single reconciliation):
  - Trigger: annualized index > 12-month baseline by > 15%
  - Remedy: One-time true-up payment/credit shared 60/40 (customer 40% of delta) with a hard cap of $120k over contract term
  - Admin: one reconciliation at month 12, simpler billing but less frequent relief

Operational notes (from Karthik): performance parity can be guaranteed via equivalence metrics (TFLOPS + memory floor). We'll include a burst bucket (20% first 6 months) with pre-agreed burst price.

Next steps: Please let us know which option you prefer by Tuesday EOD, or propose edits. If either option looks acceptable, we can slot a 30-min call next week to finalize wording for the SOW. If helpful, we can also run the Commit_Term_Scenarios.xlsx with Atlas-specific numbers (I can do that if you share expected committed units per month).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW with placeholders)
Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-Commit_Term_Scenarios

From: Thomas Reid <thomas.reid@atlashealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Jensen <sara@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Dec 2028 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — pricing protection question

Marissa —

Thanks, this is exactly what we needed. Option A (safeguard credit) looks cleaner for our CFO. Two quick asks before we sign: 1) can you confirm the exact index source name and public URL to cite in the SOW? 2) will Redwood accept the quarterly credit being applied automatically rather than requiring manual reconciliation (we prefer automatic application to avoid admin overhead).

If you can confirm those two points by Friday, we'll present to the CFO and aim to sign term sheet the week of Dec 11th.

Thomas
